rv.q: Booker prizewinning novel of the same name may not seem an intuitive choice for adaptation. It’s set over a single night in Georgetown’s Oak Hill Cemetery, where a colourful cast of limbo dwellers battle for the soul of Abraham Lincoln’s deceased 11-year-old son Willie as the president struggles to reclaim his resolve.
It's a thrilling overture to a mostly disappointing night.

cn.t: Critics split on this Met Opera adaptation of Saunders's novel, with some praising its ambitious literary scope as the company's most successful book-to-stage effort, while others find it mostly disappointing despite thrilling moments.
